outcome.technical: tests/test__locks.py only. wt3's stand-in holder no longer lets go through _unlink_quietly (a swallowed os.unlink). New _holder_lets_go(proj, said) lets go through M.release(proj, 'index', session='s-HOLD', pid=os.getppid()), the product path that retries a sharing denial via _output.while_shared, and records release's exit in `said` (a Timer's return reaches nobody). New _waited_out(proj, session) runs the timer (unchanged 0.3 s, waiter on the unchanged default bound - margin not widened) plus the waiter's acquire, joins the timer after cancel, and returns (waiter exit, seconds, holder's release exit); wt3 now uses it and prints the holder's exit in its detail. New row wt5 after wt4: clears the name, re-takes it as s-HOLD, patches os.unlink with _unlink_denied_at(real_unlink, path, 1) (one EACCES denial on the claim path only), runs _waited_out, restores os.unlink in finally, and asserts waiter exit 0, holder's release 0 and exactly two unlink attempts on the claim (one = denial swallowed, two = retried). sd2's nested unlink_of was hoisted to module-level _unlink_denied_at and sd2 now uses it (same behaviour, sd2 still PASS with (0, 3, False)). _unlink_quietly's docstring now says it clears a name with nobody reading it and is not a holder stand-in; its remaining callers (sd3, sd4, wt5's start) are fixture clears. Runs: `python3 tests/test__locks.py --selftest` in the worktree -> ALL PASS 148/148; ruff check tests/test__locks.py exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- on the file exit 0; _output_lints.prose_number_claims filtered to this file -> 0 hits. The tests.gate sweep command was not run by me (brief: own-tests, nothing of its own to run); the orchestrator's recorded run is the evidence. Dependants: .github/sweep-costs.json - still correct, it weighs test__locks.py and its blocks for sharding/timeouts and wt-block gains roughly one extra holder round trip (wt5 green ran in about 0.35 s); re-recording is optional, not required. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py - unchanged and still correct; the test now exercises its release()/while_shared path instead of bypassing it. tools/verify.sh - unchanged, names the file by path. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/audit-lock.py - unchanged, a basename reference. Class sweep: grep -rn "_unlink_quietly\|Timer(\|threading.Thread(" tests/ -> the only timer/thread letting go of a lock claim was wt3; other hits (test__panel_write _race, test_audit_usage replace wrapper, test_usage_ledger lk thread, test_panel_server servers) are not lock-claim holders. grep os.unlink/os.remove in the lock suites: test__locks pz2 (line ~541, unlink inside a patched judge on the waiter's own thread, after read_lock closed the file - no concurrent reader) and the sequential fixture clears before _write_lock, test__panel_runstate 97-98 sequential clears - left, no concurrent reader holds the claim open.
